name: Corrupt Primal of Fire

facts.text: The four Corrupt Primals rise at the waterfall bridge after the voices; Olcasgean wakes only when all four are dead. Their shared line is 'We shall protect.'
Level 83, 125,000 health, a damage shield of 80, and a trail of fire left on the ground every second.
The fire patches were softened for Living Server raids (owner, 2026-10-19); the original strength is behind a switch.

story:
Hy Brasil burns rarely, and the Sylvan fear fire more than any other thing, so it grieves them most that the Root has a fire of his own. It is the heat of rot, the kind that wakes inside a wet haystack: slow, sour and relentless. The Primal of Fire carries it on its skin, so that every blade that bites it is bitten back, and it leaves its footprints burning on the stone. Fight it where it stands and you will be standing in what it has left. Move, and keep moving, and let the healers mind the bitten hands.

Hy Brasil is a wet country and burns rarely, and the Sylvan fear fire above every other thing, because a Sylvan can burn. So it grieves them most of all that the Root has a fire of his own. It is not the bright fire of a hearth. It is the heat of rot, the warmth that wakes inside a wet haystack in autumn and smoulders for weeks until the stack goes up: slow, sour and relentless.

The guardian of fire carries that heat on its skin, so that every blade that bites it is bitten back, and it leaves its footsteps burning on the bridge stones behind it, a new patch every second. Living Server's druids have tamed the patches somewhat since the first raids, but they still burn. The fire guardian does not chase and does not hurry. It walks, and the floor it has walked on burns, and a raid that fights it in a circle ends up standing in its own fire. The Sylvan say that when it dies a smell of cut grass comes up out of the stones, as if the bridge remembered being a meadow.
legend: It burns whoever hits it, so melee needs steady heals. It leaves fire on the floor behind it: drag it in a line, never in circles, and step out of the patches. A raid that fights it in a ring ends up standing in its own fire. Veterans drag it in a long straight line along the bridge with one tank, rotate melee so no one eats the shield for too long, and keep the casters on the far side of the patches. The Sylvan add one piece of advice of their own: when it dies, do not cheer on the bridge. Say nothing, and let the stones cool.

aggro: Rot is a fire too. Slow. Patient.
The stones under it begin to smoulder: we shall protect.
The heat of rot, given legs.

loremasterTopic.text: The heat of the Root's rot, given a body. It bites back every blade that bites it and leaves its footsteps burning. Keep moving.

bookPage: Aodhan's note: I have never seen a Sylvan afraid of anything but fire, and I saw one afraid of a story about fire. The fire-keeper of Domnann, of all people, told it: the Root's fire is the slow kind, the fire that sleeps in a wet rick of hay and wakes when no one is watching. It walks at the bridge now, she said, and wherever it walks the stones burn. The realm's warriors who fought it tell me the trick is to lead it in a straight line, never round, so that the fire it leaves is behind you. The fire-keeper nodded and said that is the trick with most things.
